definition: In this source, center of gravity means the point used in judging how a structure’s mass is balanced and how stable it will be under load. A lower center of gravity is described as improving the strength and stability of the septal L-strut design.

reasons: The packet supports an engineering/biomechanics sense of center of gravity in septal L-strut modeling, not a learning or psychology/counselling sense.

The definition’s first sentence is broader than the packet’s wording; the source does not define center of gravity as a general way of judging any structure’s mass balance under load, only in the context of this specific septal design analysis.

The definition’s phrase that center of gravity is “the point used in judging how a structure’s mass is balanced” is not explicitly supported by the packet text. The packet mentions using “principles of static equilibrium, such as the center of gravity” and relates a “lower center of gravity” to “strength and stability,” but it does not describe center of gravity as a “point used” for judging “mass balance.”

Some additional implied framing (“improving the strength and stability of the septal L-strut design”) is directionally supported, but because the definition includes the unsupported “mass is balanced” characterization, the substantive claim is not defensible under the provided packet.
